summary: Brian's thesis is that edge AI — intelligence running on the device rather than in the cloud — is the next explosive chapter after the data-center buildout, with edge chips growing 30%+ a year and AI needing to leave the building to change cars, phones, homes and jobs. His seven picks: Calix (CALX, BUY), the broadband-gateway software platform that flipped from a decade of losses to record revenue and ~57% gross margins on recurring per-subscriber revenue; Nvidia (NVDA, BUY) for Jetson Thor, the on-robot brain with ~7x the prior chip's compute, plus the Isaac software and Groot robot foundation models, on top of $120B annual profit at >70% gross margin; Ambarella (AMBA, BUY), the purest edge-vision play with ~80% of revenue in edge AI, 46M+ chips shipped and a decade-long Hanwha deal, re-accelerating at 37% growth; Renesas (RNECY, BUY), the microcontroller leader putting 3nm AI into cars (R-Car X5H, 400 TOPS) — though it trades over-the-counter in the US; Broadcom (AVGO, BUY), planting a dedicated neural engine in Wi-Fi 8 routers for on-device inference alongside its data-center ASIC dominance; Mobileye (MBLY, BUY), with its EyeQ chip in 230M+ vehicles and revenue re-accelerating ~27% as a one-time writedown clears, though Intel's share overhang remains a structural risk; and Cohu (COHU, BUY), the chip tester catching the cycle turn with orders up ~57% and ~60% recurring revenue. He frames the video as only scratching the surface of edge AI, with more names to come. An Outskill AI-workshop sponsorship segment is included.
title: The Last EASY Trade Before It Explodes
